source_text: וְ/הָיָה֩ תַ֨חַת בֹּ֜שֶׂם מַ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֗ה וְ/תַ֨חַת חֲגוֹרָ֤ה נִקְפָּה֙ וְ/תַ֨חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה מִקְשֶׁה֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְ/תַ֥חַת פְּתִיגִ֖יל מַחֲגֹ֣רֶת שָׂ֑ק כִּי תַ֖חַת יֹֽפִי־׃
english_snapshot: And it shall be: instead of perfume[a], rottenness; and instead of a belt, a rope; and instead of well-set hair, baldness; and instead of a rich robe, a girding of sackcloth[c][b]; branding instead of beauty.

signals.text: The final clause is textually and lexically difficult. Many understand the sense to be 'branding instead of beauty,' while some translations render more generally 'instead of beauty, shame' or similar.

source_text: לָ֠/כֵן יִתֵּ֨ן אֲדֹנָ֥/י ה֛וּא לָ/כֶ֖ם א֑וֹת הִנֵּ֣ה הָ/עַלְמָ֗ה הָרָה֙ וְ/יֹלֶ֣דֶת בֵּ֔ן וְ/קָרָ֥את שְׁמ֖/וֹ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃
english_snapshot: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold[a], the young woman is pregnant and is bearing a son[d][c][b], and she will call his name Immanuel.

signals.text: Or 'the virgin.' The Hebrew word here is עַלְמָה ('young woman'); the Greek Septuagint renders it with a word often understood as 'virgin,' and Matthew 1:23 cites the verse in that form.
Or 'you shall call his name,' reflected in some ancient versional traditions; Matthew 1:23 has 'they shall call his name.'

source_text: הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַ/גּ֔וֹי לא הִגְדַּ֣לְתָּ הַ/שִּׂמְחָ֑ה שָׂמְח֤וּ לְ/פָנֶ֨י/ךָ֙ כְּ/שִׂמְחַ֣ת בַּ/קָּצִ֔יר כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגִ֖ילוּ בְּ/חַלְּקָ֥/ם שָׁלָֽל׃
english_snapshot: You have multiplied the nation[a]; you have not increased the joy. They rejoice before you as with the joy at harvest[b], as men exult when they divide spoil.

signals.text: Some ancient versions and many translations read, 'you have increased its joy,' reflecting a Hebrew reading like לוֹ ('to it') instead of לֹא ('not').

source_text: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑/י וּ/מַטֶּה ה֥וּא בְ/יָדָ֖/ם זַעְמִֽ/י־׃
english_snapshot: Woe to Assyria[a], the rod of my anger[b]; the staff in their hand is my wrath.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'in their hand.' Some translations render the phrase with a singular pronoun ('in his hand' or 'in its hand') to smooth the imagery, but the Masoretic Text here reads plural.

source_text: לִ/שְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּ/אַרְצִ֔/י וְ/עַל הָרַ֖/י אֲבוּסֶ֑/נּוּ וְ/סָ֤ר מֵֽ/עֲלֵי/הֶם֙ עֻלּ֔/וֹ וְ/סֻ֨בֳּל֔/וֹ מֵ/עַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖/וֹ יָסֽוּר־׃
english_snapshot: to break Assyria in my land[a], and on my mountains I will trample him; then his yoke will depart from upon them[b], and his burden from upon his shoulder will depart.

signals.text: Hebrew shifts from 'upon them' to singular 'upon his shoulder.' The singular may personify the oppressed people or function distributively.

source_text: לָ/כֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְ/מוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣/ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַ/אֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ נְכָאִֽים־־׃
english_snapshot: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail. You will moan[a] for the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth, utterly stricken.

signals.text: Or possibly, 'for the foundations of Kir-hareseth'; the Hebrew אֲשִׁישֵׁי is difficult, but the Masoretic Text most naturally reads 'raisin-cakes.'

source_text: כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔י/הָ עַד יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔י/הָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם־׃
english_snapshot: For the fields of Heshbon languish[a], the vine of Sibmah as well. The lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines; they reached as far as Jazer, they wandered into the wilderness[c][b]; its shoots spread out and crossed the sea.

signals.text: 'The sea' may refer specifically to the Dead Sea in the regional geography.

source_text: וְ/הֶאֶזְנִ֣יחוּ נְהָר֔וֹת דָּלֲל֥וּ וְ/חָרְב֖וּ יְאֹרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר קָנֶ֥ה וָ/ס֖וּף קָמֵֽלוּ׃
english_snapshot: The rivers will stink[a]; the canals of Egypt will dwindle and dry up[c][b]; reed and rush will wither.

signals.text: Or 'papyrus' for 'rush.' The Hebrew term refers to marsh vegetation associated with riverbanks.

source_text: וַ/יִּקְרָ֖א אַרְיֵ֑ה עַל מִצְפֶּ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֗/י אָנֹכִ֞י עֹמֵ֤ד תָּמִיד֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְ/עַל מִ֨שְׁמַרְתִּ֔/י אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב כָּל הַ/לֵּילֽוֹת־׀־־׃
english_snapshot: Then he cried[a], “A lion! On the watchtower, my lord, I stand continually by day[b], and at my post I am stationed all the nights.”

signals.text: Hebrew literally, “A lion!” or “Lion!” The phrase is difficult; the main text renders it as an exclamatory comparison to preserve the Masoretic reading in intelligible English.

source_text: הֵ֣ן אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָ/עָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣/הּ לְ/צִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בחיני/ו עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔י/הָ שָׂמָ֖/הּ לְ/מַפֵּלָֽה׀׃
english_snapshot: Look at the land of the Chaldeans—this is the people that was not[a]; Assyria appointed it for desert creatures. They set up their siege towers, they stripped her palaces bare[d][c][b], they made her a ruin.

signals.text: The Hebrew term behind 'siege towers' is uncertain; some render it 'watchtowers' or 'fortresses.'

source_text: נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
english_snapshot: The highways lie desolate[a]; the traveler has ceased from the road. He has broken the covenant, despised the cities[b], and regarded no man.

signals.text: Or, following some ancient versions, 'despised witnesses' instead of 'despised the cities.' The Masoretic Text reads 'cities.'

source_text: וְ/הָיָ֤ה הַ/שָּׁרָב֙ לַ/אֲגַ֔ם וְ/צִמָּא֖וֹן לְ/מַבּ֣וּעֵי מָ֑יִם בִּ/נְוֵ֤ה תַנִּים֙ רִבְצָ֔/הּ חָצִ֖יר לְ/קָנֶ֥ה וָ/גֹֽמֶא׃
english_snapshot: The burning sand will become a pool[a], and the thirsty ground springs of water; in the haunt of jackals, where they lie down, there will be grass, reeds[c][b], and rushes.

signals.text: 'Rushes' may also be rendered 'papyrus' for the Hebrew גֹמֶא.

source_text: ק֚וֹל אֹמֵ֣ר קְרָ֔א וְ/אָמַ֖ר מָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א כָּל הַ/בָּשָׂ֣ר חָצִ֔יר וְ/כָל חַסְדּ֖/וֹ כְּ/צִ֥יץ הַ/שָּׂדֶֽה־־׃
english_snapshot: A voice says[a], “Cry out!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass[c][b], and all its loveliness is like the flower of the field.

signals.text: Or, following another traditional reading: “And one said” or “And he said.”

source_text: וְ/עַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יֹצְרִ֤/י מִ/בֶּ֨טֶן֙ לְ/עֶ֣בֶד ל֔/וֹ לְ/שׁוֹבֵ֤ב יַֽעֲקֹב֙ אֵלָ֔י/ו וְ/יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לא יֵאָסֵ֑ף וְ/אֶכָּבֵד֙ בְּ/עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֵ/אלֹהַ֖/י הָיָ֥ה עֻזִּֽ/י׀׃
english_snapshot: And now Yahweh says—he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, and that Israel might be gathered to him[a]—yet I am honored in the eyes of Yahweh, and my God has become my strength.

signals.text: Hebrew consonantal text reads 'and Israel not will be gathered' (or 'though Israel is not gathered'). Many ancient interpreters and versions understand the sense as 'and Israel might be gathered to him,' which fits the parallel line 'to bring Jacob back to him.'

source_text: הִתְנַעֲרִ֧י מֵ/עָפָ֛ר ק֥וּמִי שְּׁבִ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם התפתחו מוֹסְרֵ֣י צַוָּארֵ֔/ךְ שְׁבִיָּ֖ה בַּת צִיּֽוֹן־׃ס
english_snapshot: Shake yourself from the dust[a]; rise up, sit down, Jerusalem. Loosen the bonds of your neck[c][b], captive daughter Zion.

signals.text: The Hebrew form behind 'Loosen' is difficult and irregular; it likely means 'untie yourself' or 'be loosed' from the bonds on your neck.

source_text: מֵ/עֲמַ֤ל נַפְשׁ/וֹ֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה יִשְׂבָּ֔ע בְּ/דַעְתּ֗/וֹ יַצְדִּ֥יק צַדִּ֛יק עַבְדִּ֖/י לָֽ/רַבִּ֑ים וַ/עֲוֺנֹתָ֖/ם ה֥וּא יִסְבֹּֽל׃
english_snapshot: From the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied[a]; by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many[b], and he will bear their iniquities.

signals.text: Some ancient witnesses read 'he will see light and be satisfied.' The Masoretic Text reads simply 'he will see and be satisfied.'

source_text: וְ/עַמֵּ/ךְ֙ כֻּלָּ֣/ם צַדִּיקִ֔ים לְ/עוֹלָ֖ם יִ֣ירְשׁוּ אָ֑רֶץ נֵ֧צֶר מטע/ו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֖/י לְ/הִתְפָּאֵֽר׃
english_snapshot: And all your people will be righteous[a]; forever they will possess the land, the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands[c][b], that I may be glorified.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'the shoot of his planting.' Some interpreters or textual traditions smooth this to 'my planting' because the next phrase reads 'the work of my hands,' but the main text preserves the person shift of the Masoretic Text.

source_text: כִּֽי יִבְעַ֤ל בָּחוּר֙ בְּתוּלָ֔ה יִבְעָל֖וּ/ךְ בָּנָ֑יִ/ךְ וּ/מְשׂ֤וֹשׂ חָתָן֙ עַל כַּלָּ֔ה יָשִׂ֥ישׂ עָלַ֖יִ/ךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִ/ךְ־־׃
english_snapshot: For as a young man marries a virgin[a], so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so your God will rejoice over you.

signals.text: Or, following an alternate reading reflected by some ancient versions and many interpreters, 'so your builder(s) will marry you.' The Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'your sons.'

source_text: כִּ/קְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים מַ֚יִם תִּבְעֶה אֵ֔שׁ לְ/הוֹדִ֥יעַ שִׁמְ/ךָ֖ לְ/צָרֶ֑י/ךָ מִ/פָּנֶ֖י/ךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ־׃
english_snapshot: As when fire kindles brushwood[a], and fire causes water to boil, to make your name known to your adversaries[c][b], so that nations tremble at your presence—

signals.text: In some English versifications, this line is numbered as Isaiah 63:19b.
